title: Arcana Famiglia

routes.title: パーチェルート
routes.notes: Parche (パーチェ), Clubs department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Consistently recommended as the first or an early route by both a full walkthrough (choro-game.com) and a review/impressions blog (manga-daisuki.net). Has multiple endings (ED1/ED2/ED3 pattern per choro-game), including a defeat/bad ending tied to losing the final デュエロ (duel).

routes.title: デビトルート
routes.notes: Debito (デビト), Coins department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 2nd route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ルカルート
routes.notes: Luca (ルカ). Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 3rd route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ノヴァルート
routes.notes: Nova (ノヴァ), Holy Chalice department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 4th route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: リベルタルート
routes.notes: Libertà (リベルタ). Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 5th route (last of the 5 always-open routes) by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ジョーリィルート
prerequisites: 初期5人のうち誰か1人のルートをクリアし、2周目以降に進む
routes.notes: Jolly ordinary route unlocks on the second playthrough after any one completed run. Parche is only the first recommended route, not a required character clear. Jolly is placed before Dante to support later special-ending collection.

routes.title: ダンテルート
prerequisites: 初期5人のうち誰か1人のルートをクリアし、2周目以降に進む
routes.notes: Dante ordinary route unlocks on the second playthrough after any one completed run; all six character clears are not needed for Dante ED1/ED2/ED3. The distinct Famiglia, Normal, and Defeat special endings unlock only after clearing all other characters. Dante is recommended last for this ending-collection condition, not as a route-entry lock.

sources.title: アルカナ・ファミリア -La storia della Arcana Famiglia- Ancora 攻略 (choro / 乙女ゲーム攻略ブログ)
sources.notes: Complete guide hub for the PS Vita 'Ancora' port (same VNDB entry v8203 as Rinato), linking to full individual choice-by-choice walkthroughs for all 7 routes: Liberta (blog-entry-1309.html), Nova (blog-entry-1367.html), Debito (blog-entry-1311.html), Parche (blog-entry-1368.html), Luca (blog-entry-1284.html), Dante (blog-entry-1364.html), Jolly (blog-entry-1334.html). Each page contains dated (4/1–6/1) choice text, SAVE1/SAVE2/SAVE3 markers, デュエロ (duel) success/fail outcomes (△/□/×), and ED1/ED2/ED3 ending labels. Confirms Dante's route restriction ('２周目以降ルート解放') and that his 3 special endings (ファミリアED/ノーマルED/敗北ED) require all other 6 characters cleared first ('全員を攻略後ED回収が可能'). Primary source for full choice-tree content and Dante/Jolly lock confirmation.

sources.title: アルカナ・ファミリア Rinato 個別攻略 (ruRiの気ままにオタ活)
sources.notes: Complete exact-target Nintendo Switch Rinato walkthrough covering all 7 character routes. Uses Switch button notation (for example YXY where Vita/Ancora uses △□△), dated choice text, MAP/Select/Cocoaru steps, duel success/failure paths, and ending cleanup. Adopted as Set B for target-facing reconciliation; jpGuide2 excerpts are kept verbatim to this Rinato page rather than Vita symbols.

sources.title: [PSvita] アルカナ・ファミリア無印はキャラが魅力的すぎた！オススメの攻略順とキャラ別感想 (乙女ゲーム大好記)
sources.notes: Review/impressions blog (not a choice-by-choice walkthrough) but explicitly states a numbered recommended route order under the heading 'キャラクターのおすすめ攻略順': 1.パーチェ 2.デビト 3.ルカ 4.ノヴァ 5.リベルタ 6.ダンテ 7.ジョーリィ. Notes the author personally played in a different order and adds 'シナリオとしては壮大なネタバレなどもないので、好きな順番でプレイしたら良いと思う' (no major spoilers between routes, so preferred order is fine) for the 5 unlocked routes. Used as supplementary corroboration for the first 5 routes' order; its Dante-before-Jolly placement is treated as lower-confidence than the two full walkthroughs' explicit unlock-condition text (see disagreements).

sources.title: Arcana Famiglia - VNDB entry v8203
sources.notes: Reference only. VNDB v8203 groups the October 2011 PSP original, December 2015 PS Vita Ancora port, and July 2025 Nintendo Switch / 2026 Steam Rinato releases under one work. Sharing a VNDB work id does NOT prove identical route choices, exact prompt appearance, saved-state behavior, or release-specific walkthrough applicability. The Ancora/Vita guides are Set A comparators only; each material claim must be reconciled against the exact-target Rinato/Switch Set B and unresolved differences remain blocked as documented above.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch/Steam『アルカナ・ファミリア Rinato』公式サイト - STORY

sources.title: アルカナ・ファミリア Ancora ジョーリィ 攻略 (pandaihuku)
sources.notes: Supplemental directly inspected Vita Jolly route: 4/3 directly proceeds to 剣待機室 MAP and choices, without duplicate 何かあるの？. No claim that this guide reproduces the Rinato route's entire previous-playthrough state.

disagreements: 1) Dante vs. Jolly final order: manga-daisuki.net (a review/impressions blog, not a full choice-tree walkthrough) lists its personal recommended order as ...リベルタ→ダンテ→ジョーリィ (Dante 6th, Jolly last/7th). However, both of the two full choice-by-choice walkthroughs used as primary sources (choro-game.com and ruRi hatenablog) independently state that Dante's three notable endings (ファミリアED / ノーマルED / 敗北ED, including the Famiglia End '第10のカード ルオータ・デラ・フォルトゥナ') can only be obtained '全員を攻略後' (after clearing everyone/all other characters) — which includes Jolly. This condition gates Dante's special endings only, not ordinary Dante route access. Both Dante and Jolly become selectable on a second playthrough after any first clear. We recommend Dante last so the special endings can be collected without another replay. 2) Whether Dante's Famiglia ED constitutes a distinct 'true end' separate from a normal character route: no source uses the exact phrase 真エンド (true end), but the gating of the Famiglia ED behind clearing all other 6 routes, plus its explicit '第10のカード' (10th/final tarot card) framing distinguishing it from the other 6 characters' single-route endings, matches the standard 'true end' pattern used elsewhere in this repository's guides; it is flagged is_true_ending on the dante route on that basis. 3) The first 5 routes (Parche, Debito, Luca, Nova, Liberta) have no documented mechanical locks or prerequisites in either full walkthrough — the order used here follows manga-daisuki.net's suggested order for lack of any conflicting source, and could be freely reordered among themselves without affecting route access. 4) momokan.chu.jp and the PSP-era wiki at arcana.stgtk.com could not be directly fetched (DNS resolution failures for both domains during this session) despite appearing in search results; their content is treated as unverified/supplementary and was not used as a primary source. No English guide was located or used; per the brief, Japanese sources take full precedence and none was needed as even a supplementary reference given two solid full Japanese walkthroughs were found. 5) Revalidation note (2026-09-25): Set A remains the directly inspected Ancora/Vita walkthrough at choro-game.com, while Set B is now a directly inspected exact-target Rinato/Nintendo Switch walkthrough at ruRi. Rinato release documentation identifies the Switch title as a port of Ancora and the exact-target Set B provides target-platform choice/duel text. Exact-target disagreements, including the Jolly ordinary-choice difference documented above, are preserved rather than silently normalized. 6) ED2 version differences (2026-10-09): Debito ED2 MAP differs: Set A (Ancora) selects リベルタ; exact-target Set B (Rinato) selects ダンテ. Target-facing route follows Set B and uses the Set-A omission marker. Luca ED2 Save1 is later in Set A than in Set B; use the earlier Set-B checkpoint and do not fabricate matching Set-A evidence. The missing ED2 and explicit ED3 ending terminals were restored in all affected route files. All modified routes require independent structural and accuracy re-review. 7) Dante Normal ED intermediate prompt (2026-10-23): Set A (Ancora/Vita choro) includes `何も失いたくない。でも、パーパも失えない` between the successful June 1 duel and tenth-card choice on its Save2 replay. The directly inspected exact-target Rinato/Switch Set B (ruRi) documents `SAVE2 → 6/1までシナリオスキップ → デュエロ XXXYAX 成功 → 第１０のカード → ノーマルED` without that intermediate prompt. Its appearance in the identical Switch Save2/skip state is NOT independently established, so the guide no longer makes it a mandatory step; if the player encounters it, the Set-A answer is supplied as an optional contingency in `enGuide`. Do not claim the prompt never exists in Rinato. Fresh independent Dante structural and accuracy review is required for this route-topology change. 8) Consolidated Rinato/Switch source-literal audit (2026-10-23): Reviewed all 51 A2 choice-literal discrepancies across Parche (5), Debito (9), Luca (11), Nova (5), Liberta (9), Jolly (4), and Dante (8) against the existing Set-B ruRi transcription and directly inspected ruRi Rinato/Switch walkthrough (https://ruri-ototgame.hatenablog.com/entry/2025/12/30/225051). Target-facing simpleJp now preserves the Set-B wording, including leading/trailing ellipses, commas, and punctuation; Ancora/Vita source text remains intact in jpGuide1. Also fixed Luca's Set-B-confirmed 5/3 spacing in 「ルカ！肉！！」 (former step 115). All unchanged choice/action source lanes were retained. 9) Unverified Set-A-only main-path prompts (2026-10-23): On 4/3, the older Ancora/Vita Set A includes a second 「何かあるの？」 immediately before the Luca MAP action in Parche, Debito, Luca, Liberta, and Jolly. The exact-target ruRi Set B documents 4/3 MAP→next choices directly and does not show that intermediate prompt. Other disputed Set-A-only choices include Parche's 「ちょっとおもしろそう」 and Liberta's 「……コンフェットゥーラ……私も好きだよ？」. Nova is a distinct, confirmed date/choice alignment defect rather than an omitted intermediate prompt before 5/22: direct inspection of Set A (https://choro-game.com/e/arcana-ancora-guide-nova) shows 5/22 「子どもは好き？」 followed on 5/23, after the MAP, by 「……答えられない」; exact-target Set B (https://ruri-ototgame.hatenablog.com/entry/2025/12/30/225051) instead shows 5/22 「ずっと心配だった」 and 5/23 「子どもは好き？」 after its MAP. Corrected Nova to follow Set-B's player-facing action on each date (5/22 now 「ずっと心配だった」, with the older Set-A text retained in jpGuide1; 5/23 now includes 「子どもは好き？」, retaining Set A's different 5/23 text in jpGuide1). Removed the inaccurate 5/22 claim that 「……答えられない」 might precede 「無理ならいい……」; the date-specific difference is explained at the 5/23 step. This establishes what the inspected walkthroughs actually print, NOT identical playthrough state or universal Switch prompt conditions. Remaining Set-A-only prompts are not presented as unconditional Rinato actions; conditional hints are retained only when attached to the right dated action. These omissions do NOT establish that the prompt is absent on every Switch save/branch state. Exact same-state Switch occurrence/conditions are still unverified, so retain this source-state blocker and request independent structural + accuracy re-review of affected route/research pairs; do not assert PASS or reviewed:true. 10) Additional directly inspected Japanese supplemental route corpus (2026-10-23): maistar.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-2697.html explicitly covers Rinato/Switch and Ancora/Vita, with separate route pages for all seven characters (URLs in sources). Parche/Debito/Luca/Liberta/Jolly all show a 4/3 Luca MAP directly after their 4/2 sequence, without the extra Ancora Set-A 4/3 何かあるの？. Parche 4/6 documents ちょっとおもしろそう, but 4/7 lists only the Parche MAP; Nova is not simply omitting a 5/22 prompt: Set A places 「……答えられない」 at the 5/23 map, and Set B uses a different 5/22 choice followed by 「子どもは好き？」 on 5/23 (see item 9); Dante's supplemental maistar Switch-labeled Normal ED path explicitly lists the extra post-duel prompt after duel XXXYAX, whereas the designated exact-target ruRi Set B Save2/skip sequence omits it; maistar resumes from its earlier Save1 and selects different 5/27–5/31 MAPs, so the two paths do not establish identical preceding state or the prompt condition for this guide's Save14. The early-route maistar omissions corroborate the Set-B-first presentation for those paths, while its Switch Normal ED explicitly shows Dante's additional prompt can occur on a different Switch route state. Neither source comparison is direct gameplay/capture or proof of the precise prompt conditions for this guide's preceding state: some maistar 4/1/4/2 choices differ, Liberta 4/12 uses a different MAP destination, and Dante's Save1 Normal ED is not the guide's Save14/ruRi Save2 skip. Keep A3 and Dante same-state applicability explicitly unresolved. These are supplemental evidence, not substitutes for Set A/B, and do not authorize unconditional deletion/restoration or PASS. 11) Additional independent directly inspected Vita corpus (2026-10-30): https://pandaihuku.blog.fc2.com/blog-entry-332.html and its seven character pages (sources above) supply a third independently authored Japanese walkthrough. In Parche, Debito, Luca, Liberta, Jolly (and also Nova/Dante), 4/2 shows 「何かあるの？」 but 4/3 starts at the 剣待機室 MAP without choro's second identical question. This corroborates the exact-target ruRi Rinato Set B presentation and makes a choro-specific duplication/choice-state issue more plausible than a categorical Vita-to-Switch text change, but it is not a directly observed Rinato same-state test. More decisively for Nova, this Vita author independently places 「ずっと心配だった」 on 5/22 and 「子どもは好き？」 on 5/23, matching exact Rinato Set B and disagreeing with choro's dated placements. The current Nova route now uses the directly supported Rinato dates and the older choro quotes remain lane-specific; its 5/22 misplaced optional hint was removed. The pandaihuku Ancora index's all-character Normal ED skips from 5/31 to 6/1 without printing choro's post-duel prompt, but a separate Switch-labeled maistar path does print it from its Save1; neither substitutes for Switch capture/fully matched hidden state from this guide's Save14. Evidence strengthens the source reconciliation but does not constitute an independent accuracy PASS or owner-approved exception for remaining exact-state blockers.
